records.prompt: The dots mark equal time intervals. Describe the motion shown, connect the changing spacing to velocity, and critique the claim “equal time intervals always mean constant velocity.”
choices: The object is slowing down; changing dot spacing means the velocity magnitude changes. Equal time intervals do not imply constant velocity.
The object must have constant velocity because times are equal.
Dot spacing shows mass, not motion.
The diagram gives no information about motion.
records.answer: The object is slowing down; changing dot spacing means the velocity magnitude changes. Equal time intervals do not imply constant velocity.
records.solution: In a motion diagram made at equal time intervals, larger spacing means greater speed. Changing spacing is evidence of changing velocity.
